comments.author: aallennnn
comments.content:
This issue is having multiple stages. First stage is where tor browser blocked ubuntu.com from downloading some suspicious file in the same time when Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS iso file downloading is initiated. After download is done, hash signature verification was successful. After installation, suspicious hidden file is found at location /etc/.resolv.conf.systemd-resolved.bak. File is including dns records which are pointing to private ip addresses: nameserver 10.131.53.11, nameserver 10.131.53.12, nameserver 10.131.53.13 and domain search ppa openstack.prodstack5.lan. These ip addresses are not some kind of loopback ip addresses like 127.0.0.53:53 which are known as part of dns configuration. I wasn't able to find this file in available Ubuntu documentation.

There is one more hidden file which is also unknown to me: etc/.updated . Content can be found on screen shot in attachment. I tried this command you sent me on this another file as well and I'm getting same result.

I have my third party DNS configured in /etc/systemd/resolved.conf and in this file there is no issues. I'm using DNS over TLS.

This file can be very dangerous if someone would connect host with same private IP address like from file.

comments.author: puida
comments.content:
I think this file is somehow a leftover artifact of the image building process. I downloaded the ubuntu-26.04.1-desktop-amd64.iso and mounted the inner minimal.squashfs

% ls -la /tmp/iso/squash/etc/.resolv.conf.systemd-resolved.bak
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 862 Aug 26 02:27 /tmp/iso/squash/etc/.resolv.conf.systemd-resolved.bak

% cat /tmp/iso/squash/etc/.resolv.conf.systemd-resolved.bak
# This is /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf managed by man:systemd-resolved(8).
# Do not edit.
#
# This file might be symlinked as /etc/resolv.conf. If you're looking at
# /etc/resolv.conf and seeing this text, you have followed the symlink.
#
# This is a dynamic resolv.conf file for connecting local clients directly to
# all known uplink DNS servers. This file lists all configured search domains.
#
# Third party programs should typically not access this file directly, but only
# through the symlink at /etc/resolv.conf. To manage man:resolv.conf(5) in a
# different way, replace this symlink by a static file or a different symlink.
#
# See man:systemd-resolved.service(8) for details about the supported modes of
# operation for /etc/resolv.conf.

nameserver 10.131.53.11
nameserver 10.131.53.12
nameserver 10.131.53.13
search ppa openstack.prodstack5.lan

I don't think this is a dnsmasq bug at all. Should this be a task in livecd-rootfs? Unsure what actually generate those images.
